minutes.headline: ZBA granted a variance for a 16% driveway at 321 Sunny Hill Road, on a 4-1 vote, over a 12% bylaw limit.
minutes.summary: The board heard CTB Holdings LLC's request for a variance from the 12% maximum driveway grade for a newly built, already paved driveway at 321 Sunny Hill Road. Discussion covered the building commissioner's timeline of ignored requests for grades, the site's steep topography and soils, and the possible remedy of ripping out the driveway. The variance was granted, and a hearing for 485 Shirley Road was continued to May 8 at 7 p.m.

public_comment.topic: Spoke in favor of the variance. He explained why builders keep the driveway level at the bottom and top, said fire trucks can manage grades like this, and compared it to other towns' driveways.

votes.motion: Approve the variance from the 12% maximum driveway grade at 321 Sunny Hill Road, finding no substantial detriment to the public good and no nullification of the bylaw's intent.
Continue the 485 Shirley Road hearing to May 8 at 7:00 p.m.

budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant argued that regrading would force the owners to pay for paving a second time, which is the financial hardship claim.
A member noted the bylaw allows a daily fine for violations and suggested a fine might be imposed for ignoring the bylaw. It was not acted on.

decisions.decision: The hearing for 485 Shirley Road, requested by the applicant's attorney, was continued to May 8 at 7 p.m.
The variance carries standard conditions: compliance with all applicable laws and regulations, periodic review, filing with the town clerk within 14 days, and recording at the registry of deeds.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted a variance from the 12% maximum driveway grade for a newly built, already paved driveway at 321 Sunny Hill Road, 4-1.
The variance carries standard conditions: legal compliance, periodic review, filing with the town clerk within 14 days, and recording at the registry of deeds.
The applicant argued that regrading would mean paying for paving a second time, which was its financial hardship claim.
A member noted the bylaw allows a daily fine for violations and suggested one might be imposed; it was not acted on.
The hearing for 485 Shirley Road was continued to May 8 at 7 p.m. at the applicant's attorney's request.

why_it_matters: The decision lets a driveway steeper than the bylaw's 12% limit stand after it was built, which shows how the board treats work done before relief was sought and bears on how the grade limit is enforced elsewhere in town.
The daily-fine provision was raised and not used, so no penalty for building before approval was set in this case.
